answer.reason: The Court dismissed certiorari as improvidently granted, so the Ninth Circuit's class certification stands. The only money figure is the dissent's potential damages of about $500M per year (about 3% of the $16.4B non-affiliate market value, which scores 1 on the A rubric). However, the figure is a per-year ceiling stated by the dissent, not a consequence the ruling decided, so I scored A at 2 on a multi-year reading; the case concerns kiosk accessibility at patient service centers, a peripheral practice rather than a core product or pricing practice, and the 10-Q names the Davis v. LabCorp case in its contingencies note.
